what_this_is: Per-fund facts that Form N-PORT does not carry, for the four retail families audited in docs/research/alternative-sleeves-audit.md: dividend and dividend-growth, REITs, buffer / defined-outcome, and spot bitcoin. Expense ratios, inception dates, indices, the prospectus's standardised average-annual-total-return table including its after-tax rows, and the fiscal-year distribution tax character. Every figure is read from the fund's own SEC-filed document, never from a sponsor marketing page, because a filing carries an accession number, a filing date and an immutable document.
after_tax_methodology: Item 4(b)(2)(iii) of Form N-1A. After-tax returns are computed by the fund using the HIGHEST individual federal marginal income and capital-gains rates in effect at the time of each distribution, and reflect NO state or local tax. They assume a taxable account and are irrelevant to an IRA. They are the fund's own figures, not this repository's estimate. Two funds' tables end 2024-12-31 and the rest end 2025-12-31; a drag computed across that line is not a like-for-like comparison and the period is stated on every row.
period_mismatch_note: SCHD, DGRO, NOBL and USRT report through 2024-12-31 because their fiscal years end 8/31, 4/30, 5/31 and 4/30 respectively, so their annual prospectus update lands using the last completed calendar year. This was checked on 2026-08-17: no newer table exists. It is a genuine absence, not an access failure. VTI and VOO are therefore recorded at BOTH period ends so that every comparison has a period-matched control.
no_threshold_uses_these: Every after-tax figure here was read while assembling this file and before any verdict was written. No falsifier in this study is placed on them; they are measured and reported.
unreachable: SCHD 30-day SEC yield and trailing distribution yield: schwabassetmanagement.com returned HTTP 403 to an automated client on 2026-08-17 and the figure appears in no SEC filing. Bot protection was not circumvented. The distribution yield below is COMPUTED from the fund's own N-CSR distribution total and net assets instead, and is labelled as such.
NOBL qualified-dividend-income percentage: the ProShares N-CSR states only that the fund 'designated up to the maximum amount' with no per-fund figure. Not found.

Qualified-dividend / Section 199A / dividends-received-deduction split for VNQ, SCHH and USRT: the N-CSR tax notes report only ordinary income, long-term gain and return of capital. The 199A share lives in each issuer's year-end tax-character statement, which was not retrieved. Not found. This matters and it runs in the REITs' favour: a REIT dividend eligible for the 20% Section 199A deduction is taxed below the ordinary rate, so every REIT tax figure in this study is an UPPER bound on the cost.
POCT's inaugural 2018 outcome-period starting cap: no 497K located for that period. Not found.
POCT's net-of-fee cap for the 2025-10-01 period: only the gross 11.81% was extracted. Not found.

FT Vest starting caps for the twelve funds inside BUFR and BUFD: not retrieved. The buffer levels were (10% for BUFR's underlying funds, -5% to -30% for BUFD's) and are recorded; the caps are not found, so no cap-pricing figure in this study is attributed to BUFR.

distribution_character.yield_note: COMPUTED here as ordinary income divided by fiscal-year-end net assets, both from the same N-CSR. It is not a published yield and is not the SEC 30-day yield.

distribution_character.note: The report designates the qualified amount 'for calendar year 2024' while the identically formatted VIG note says 2025. Quoted as filed; not corrected.
ProShares reports tax character on an October 31 tax year, distinct from the May 31 financial-reporting year. The qualified share is not disclosed.

BUFD.buffer_note: A deep buffer absorbs losses BETWEEN -5% and -30%, so the first 5% of loss is borne by the shareholder and the buffered band is 25 points wide. It is not comparable with a 10% or 15% first-loss buffer and is not priced with them here.

PJUL.starting_caps_note: Each figure is taken from that outcome period's own Innovator 497K summary prospectus and is GROSS of the 0.79% fee. The 2018-08-08 entry is the inaugural stub period.
PJUL.no_dividend_quote: If the Fund invests solely in FLEX Options that reference the Underlying ETF, the Cap and Buffer will be provided on a price return basis (i.e., the returns will be provided based on changes in the share price of the Underlying ETF), and the Fund will not receive the benefit of any dividends.
PJUL.buffer_only_over_full_period_quote: The Fund's strategy seeks to provide the sought-after protection of the Buffer if Shares are held at the time at which the Fund enters into the FLEX Options and held until those FLEX Options expire at the end of the Outcome Period. In the event an investor purchases Shares after the FLEX Options were entered into or sells Shares prior to the expiration of the FLEX Options, the Buffer that the Fund seeks to provide may not be available.
PJUL.multi_period_quote: the imposition of a new Cap on future gains in subsequent Outcome Periods may make it difficult to recoup any losses from the prior Outcome Periods such that, over multiple Outcome Periods, the Fund may have losses that exceed those of the Underlying ETF.

IBIT.name: iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF
IBIT.structure: Delaware statutory trust registered under the Securities Act; NOT a registered investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940 and NOT a commodity pool under the CEA. It files 10-K and 10-Q and has never filed a Form N-PORT, N-CSR or N-CEN.
IBIT.structure_quote: The Trust is not registered as an investment company for purposes of U.S. federal securities laws and is not subject to regulation by the SEC as an investment company. Consequently, the owners of Shares do not have the regulatory protections provided to investors in registered investment companies.
IBIT.fee_waiver: 0.12% on the first $5.0bn of trust assets, from listing through 2025-01-10. EXPIRED. FY2025 expenses were 0.25% before and after waiver; only $178,082 was waived in FY2025 against $5,958,429 in FY2024.
IBIT.listing_approval: SEC Release 34-99306, 2024-01-10, granting accelerated approval to eleven spot bitcoin ETP listings
IBIT.nav_index: CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate - New York Variant, administered by CF Benchmarks Ltd. (FCA-regulated). Observation window 3-4 p.m. ET, twelve 5-minute volume-weighted medians equally averaged, across Bitstamp, Coinbase, itBit, Kraken, Gemini, LMAX Digital, Crypto.com and Bullish.
IBIT.custodian: Coinbase Custody Trust Company, LLC, with Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. as an additional available custodian; Coinbase, Inc. as prime execution agent, an affiliate of the custodian
IBIT.distributions: none. 'The Trust did not declare any cash distributions to Shareholders during the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.' The sponsor's fee is paid by selling or delivering bitcoin, which is itself a taxable event for holders.
IBIT.tax_treatment: Grantor trust, opinion of Clifford Chance US LLP, 'although not free from doubt due to the lack of directly governing authority'. Holders are treated as owning a pro rata share of the bitcoin directly. Most trust expenses are miscellaneous itemized deductions and are therefore not deductible by individuals.
IBIT.collectibles_rate: NOT FOUND, and this is a clean negative. The words 'collectible' and '28%' appear nowhere in either trust's 10-K tax discussion, and EDGAR full-text search over the whole registrant history returns zero hits for IBIT. The filings say only that bitcoin is property that may be held as a capital asset and that the treatment is uncertain and may change with retroactive effect. Do NOT attribute a collectibles position to these filings.
